chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from Fadalah narrated from Fadalah ibn Ayyub, from al-'Ala' ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:
I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): A man prayed the dawn prayer when the dawn rose, so he said: 'There is no harm.'

key_terms.طَلَعَ: Rose / Emerged (referring to the appearance of true dawn)
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: There is no harm / It is permissible

ai.seo_question: Is it valid to pray Fajr prayer at the exact moment dawn breaks?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, the Imam confirms the validity of praying Fajr at the precise moment of true dawn (al-fajr al-sadiq), addressing the scholarly nuance of whether one must wait for the sun's upper limb to appear. This ruling is significant in Shia jurisprudence as it distinguishes the start of the prayer time from the time of *karaahah* (disliked delay), emphasizing that the obligation begins immediately upon the appearance of the horizontal twilight. It reflects the practical application of Quranic commands to observe prayers at their appointed times without unnecessary delay.
